Summary

COUSR02C is a CICS online program within the CardDemo application that provides the functionality to update an existing user's information in the USRSEC security file. The program allows an administrator to look up a user by User ID and modify their first name, last name, password, and user type, validating all fields before saving changes. It operates as a Main/Driver program, managing its own screen interactions and navigating to other programs such as COADM01C via XCTL transfers.
- **Execution Environment**: Online (CICS) - **Database Access**: VSAM/CICS File (USRSEC) - **MQ Calls**: No - **Module Type**: Main module
### Key Functionalities: 1: Session Initialization Check - When the program is first launched with no communication area, redirect the user to the sign-on screen (COSGN00C) to ensure a valid session exists before allowing any user update operations. 2: Initial Screen Load with Pre-selected User - On the first entry into the update screen, if a user ID has already been selected from a previous screen (CDEMO-CU02-USR-SELECTED), automatically populate the User ID field and look up the user's details to pre-fill the update form. 3: Display User Update Screen - Present the user update form to the operator, including header information (current date, time, transaction ID, program name), any error or informational messages, and the user data fields (User ID, First Name, Last Name, Password, User Type). 4: Receive User Input from Screen - Capture all data entered by the operator on the user update form, including User ID and any modified fields for First Name, Last Name, Password, and User Type. 5: Validate User ID on Lookup - When the operator presses Enter to look up a user, validate that the User ID field is not empty. If empty, display the error message 'User ID can NOT be empty...' and prompt the operator to enter a valid User ID. 6: Look Up User Record - Using the entered User ID, retrieve the existing user record from the user security file. If the user is found, display a message prompting the operator to press PF5 to save updates. If the user is not found, display 'User ID NOT found...' error message. 7: Populate Screen with Existing User Data - After successfully retrieving the user record, populate the update form fields with the user's current First Name, Last Name, Password, and User Type so the operator can review and modify them. 8: Validate All Required Fields Before Update - Before saving changes, validate that none of the required fields (User ID, First Name, Last Name, Password, User Type) are empty. Display specific error messages for each missing field: 'User ID can NOT be empty...', 'First Name can NOT be empty...', 'Last Name can NOT be empty...', 'Password can NOT be empty...', 'User Type can NOT be empty...' 9: Detect Changes to User Data - Compare each entered field value (First Name, Last Name, Password, User Type) against the current values stored in the user security file to determine if any modifications have been made by the operator. 10: Save Updated User Information - If one or more fields have been modified, write the updated user record back to the user security file and display a success message in green: 'User [ID] has been updated ...' 11: No Changes Detected Warning - If the operator attempts to save but no fields have been changed from their current values, display the message 'Please modify to update ...' in red to inform the operator that no update is needed. 12: Save and Return to Previous Screen (PF3) - When the operator presses PF3, attempt to save any user modifications and then navigate back to the calling program. If no calling program is identified, return to the administration screen (COADM01C). 13: Clear Screen Fields (PF4) - When the operator presses PF4, clear all input fields on the update form (User ID, First Name, Last Name, Password, User Type) and reset any messages, allowing the operator to start fresh. 14: Save User Updates (PF5) - When the operator presses PF5, validate all required fields and save any modifications made to the user's First Name, Last Name, Password, or User Type in the user security file. 15: Return to Administration Screen (PF12) - When the operator presses PF12, navigate back to the main administration screen (COADM01C) without saving any changes. 16: Invalid Key Handling - If the operator presses any key other than the supported function keys (Enter, PF3, PF4, PF5, PF12), display an invalid key message to inform the operator of the valid key options. 17: Return to Previous Screen Navigation - Transfer control back to the appropriate calling program, passing along the current session and communication data, defaulting to the sign-on screen if no calling program is specified.

1. **Initializing and Sending the Screen (SEND-USRUPD-SCREEN)** ```cobol SEND-USRUPD-SCREEN. PERFORM POPULATE-HEADER-INFO MOVE WS-MESSAGE TO ERRMSGO OF COUSR2AO EXEC CICS SEND MAP('COUSR2A') MAPSET('COUSR02') FROM(COUSR2AO) ERASE CURSOR END-EXEC. ``` This paragraph populates the header fields and error message, then sends the COUSR2A map to the terminal. --- 2. **Receiving Input from the Screen (RECEIVE-USRUPD-SCREEN)** ```cobol RECEIVE-USRUPD-SCREEN. EXEC CICS RECEIVE MAP('COUSR2A') MAPSET('COUSR02') INTO(COUSR2AI) RESP(WS-RESP-CD) RESP2(WS-REAS-CD) END-EXEC. ``` This paragraph receives user input from the COUSR2A map into the COUSR2AI input structure. --- 3. **Populating Header Fields (POPULATE-HEADER-INFO)** ```cobol POPULATE-HEADER-INFO. MOVE FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE TO WS-CURDATE-DATA MOVE CCDA-TITLE01 TO TITLE01O OF COUSR2AO MOVE CCDA-TITLE02 TO TITLE02O OF COUSR2AO MOVE WS-TRANID TO TRNNAMEO OF COUSR2AO MOVE WS-PGMNAME TO PGMNAMEO OF COUSR2AO MOVE WS-CURDATE-MONTH TO WS-CURDATE-MM MOVE WS-CURDATE-DAY TO WS-CURDATE-DD MOVE WS-CURDATE-YEAR(3:2) TO WS-CURDATE-YY MOVE WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY TO CURDATEO OF COUSR2AO MOVE WS-CURTIME-HOURS TO WS-CURTIME-HH MOVE WS-CURTIME-MINUTE TO WS-CURTIME-MM MOVE WS-CURTIME-SECOND TO WS-CURTIME-SS MOVE WS-CURTIME-HH-MM-SS TO CURTIMEO OF COUSR2AO. ``` Populates TRNNAMEO (Transaction Name), TITLE01O (Title Line 1), TITLE02O (Title Line 2), PGMNAMEO (Program Name), CURDATEO (Current Date), and CURTIMEO (Current Time) on the screen. --- 4. **Processing the ENTER Key – Fetching User Data (PROCESS-ENTER-KEY)** ```cobol PROCESS-ENTER-KEY. EVALUATE TRUE WHEN USRIDINI OF COUSR2AI = SPACES OR LOW-VALUES MOVE 'Y' TO WS-ERR-FLG MOVE 'User ID can NOT be empty...' TO WS-MESSAGE MOVE -1 TO USRIDINL OF COUSR2AI PERFORM SEND-USRUPD-SCREEN WHEN OTHER MOVE -1 TO USRIDINL OF COUSR2AI CONTINUE END-EVALUATE IF NOT ERR-FLG-ON MOVE SPACES TO FNAMEI OF COUSR2AI LNAMEI OF COUSR2AI PASSWDI OF COUSR2AI USRTYPEI OF COUSR2AI MOVE USRIDINI OF COUSR2AI TO SEC-USR-ID PERFORM READ-USER-SEC-FILE END-IF. IF NOT ERR-FLG-ON MOVE SEC-USR-FNAME TO FNAMEI OF COUSR2AI MOVE SEC-USR-LNAME TO LNAMEI OF COUSR2AI MOVE SEC-USR-PWD TO PASSWDI OF COUSR2AI MOVE SEC-USR-TYPE TO USRTYPEI OF COUSR2AI PERFORM SEND-USRUPD-SCREEN END-IF. ``` Reads USRIDINI from the screen, validates it is not empty, reads the user record, and populates FNAMEI, LNAMEI, PASSWDI, and USRTYPEI back to the screen. --- 5. **Updating User Information – Validation and Save (UPDATE-USER-INFO)** ```cobol UPDATE-USER-INFO. EVALUATE TRUE WHEN USRIDINI OF COUSR2AI = SPACES OR LOW-VALUES MOVE 'Y' TO WS-ERR-FLG MOVE 'User ID can NOT be empty...' TO WS-MESSAGE MOVE -1 TO USRIDINL OF COUSR2AI PERFORM SEND-USRUPD-SCREEN WHEN FNAMEI OF COUSR2AI = SPACES OR LOW-VALUES MOVE 'Y' TO WS-ERR-FLG MOVE 'First Name can NOT be empty...' TO WS-MESSAGE MOVE -1 TO FNAMEL OF COUSR2AI PERFORM SEND-USRUPD-SCREEN WHEN LNAMEI OF COUSR2AI = SPACES OR LOW-VALUES MOVE 'Y' TO WS-ERR-FLG MOVE 'Last Name can NOT be empty...' TO WS-MESSAGE MOVE -1 TO LNAMEL OF COUSR2AI PERFORM SEND-USRUPD-SCREEN WHEN PASSWDI OF COUSR2AI = SPACES OR LOW-VALUES MOVE 'Y' TO WS-ERR-FLG MOVE 'Password can NOT be empty...' TO WS-MESSAGE MOVE -1 TO PASSWDL OF COUSR2AI PERFORM SEND-USRUPD-SCREEN WHEN USRTYPEI OF COUSR2AI = SPACES OR LOW-VALUES MOVE 'Y' TO WS-ERR-FLG MOVE 'User Type can NOT be empty...' TO WS-MESSAGE MOVE -1 TO USRTYPEL OF COUSR2AI PERFORM SEND-USRUPD-SCREEN WHEN OTHER MOVE -1 TO FNAMEL OF COUSR2AI CONTINUE END-EVALUATE IF NOT ERR-FLG-ON MOVE USRIDINI OF COUSR2AI TO SEC-USR-ID PERFORM READ-USER-SEC-FILE IF FNAMEI OF COUSR2AI NOT = SEC-USR-FNAME MOVE FNAMEI OF COUSR2AI TO SEC-USR-FNAME SET USR-MODIFIED-YES TO TRUE END-IF IF LNAMEI OF COUSR2AI NOT = SEC-USR-LNAME MOVE LNAMEI OF COUSR2AI TO SEC-USR-LNAME SET USR-MODIFIED-YES TO TRUE END-IF IF PASSWDI OF COUSR2AI NOT = SEC-USR-PWD MOVE PASSWDI OF COUSR2AI TO SEC-USR-PWD SET USR-MODIFIED-YES TO TRUE END-IF IF USRTYPEI OF COUSR2AI NOT = SEC-USR-TYPE MOVE USRTYPEI OF COUSR2AI TO SEC-USR-TYPE SET USR-MODIFIED-YES TO TRUE END-IF IF USR-MODIFIED-YES PERFORM UPDATE-USER-SEC-FILE ELSE MOVE 'Please modify to update ...' TO WS-MESSAGE MOVE DFHRED TO ERRMSGC OF COUSR2AO PERFORM SEND-USRUPD-SCREEN END-IF END-IF. ``` Validates all screen input fields (USRIDINI, FNAMEI, LNAMEI, PASSWDI, USRTYPEI), compares them with stored values, and triggers the update if any field has changed. Displays appropriate error messages via ERRMSGO. --- 6. **Clearing the Screen (INITIALIZE-ALL-FIELDS)** ```cobol INITIALIZE-ALL-FIELDS. MOVE -1 TO USRIDINL OF COUSR2AI MOVE SPACES TO USRIDINI OF COUSR2AI FNAMEI OF COUSR2AI LNAMEI OF COUSR2AI PASSWDI OF COUSR2AI USRTYPEI OF COUSR2AI WS-MESSAGE. ``` Clears all input fields on the screen (User ID, First Name, Last Name, Password, User Type) and the message area, then resets cursor to the User ID field. --- 7. **Initial Screen Display on First Entry (MAIN-PARA)** ```cobol IF NOT CDEMO-PGM-REENTER SET CDEMO-PGM-REENTER TO TRUE MOVE LOW-VALUES TO COUSR2AO MOVE -1 TO USRIDINL OF COUSR2AI IF CDEMO-CU02-USR-SELECTED NOT = SPACES AND LOW-VALUES MOVE CDEMO-CU02-USR-SELECTED TO USRIDINI OF COUSR2AI PERFORM PROCESS-ENTER-KEY END-IF PERFORM SEND-USRUPD-SCREEN ``` On first entry, initializes the screen output area, sets cursor to User ID field, and if a user was pre-selected from a prior screen, pre-populates the User ID field and fetches the user data automatically. --- 8. **Error Message Display in READ-USER-SEC-FILE** ```cobol EVALUATE WS-RESP-CD WHEN DFHRESP(NORMAL) MOVE 'Press PF5 key to save your updates ...' TO WS-MESSAGE MOVE DFHNEUTR TO ERRMSGC OF COUSR2AO PERFORM SEND-USRUPD-SCREEN WHEN DFHRESP(NOTFND) MOVE 'Y' TO WS-ERR-FLG MOVE 'User ID NOT found...' TO WS-MESSAGE MOVE -1 TO USRIDINL OF COUSR2AI PERFORM SEND-USRUPD-SCREEN WHEN OTHER MOVE 'Y' TO WS-ERR-FLG MOVE 'Unable to lookup User...' TO WS-MESSAGE MOVE -1 TO FNAMEL OF COUSR2AI PERFORM SEND-USRUPD-SCREEN END-EVALUATE. ``` After reading the user record, updates ERRMSGO with status messages and sets ERRMSGC color accordingly. --- 9. **Success/Failure Message Display in UPDATE-USER-SEC-FILE** ```cobol EVALUATE WS-RESP-CD WHEN DFHRESP(NORMAL) MOVE SPACES TO WS-MESSAGE MOVE DFHGREEN TO ERRMSGC OF COUSR2AO STRING 'User ' DELIMITED BY SIZE SEC-USR-ID DELIMITED BY SPACE ' has been updated ...' DELIMITED BY SIZE INTO WS-MESSAGE PERFORM SEND-USRUPD-SCREEN WHEN DFHRESP(NOTFND) MOVE 'Y' TO WS-ERR-FLG MOVE 'User ID NOT found...' TO WS-MESSAGE MOVE -1 TO USRIDINL OF COUSR2AI PERFORM SEND-USRUPD-SCREEN WHEN OTHER MOVE 'Y' TO WS-ERR-FLG MOVE 'Unable to Update User...' TO WS-MESSAGE MOVE -1 TO FNAMEL OF COUSR2AI PERFORM SEND-USRUPD-SCREEN END-EVALUATE. ``` After the update operation, displays a green success message (e.g., "User USERID has been updated ...") or an appropriate error message in ERRMSGO.
